project_rationale: PureCLIP's peak-calling quality for eCLIP data is highly sensitive to several numerical parameters (bandwidth, merge distance, filtering thresholds) whose optimal values are dataset-dependent and cannot be determined analytically. Manual grid search is impractical given that a single PureCLIP run on a full genome takes hours. This project automates the search: an optimizer (either an LLM reasoning from prior biological knowledge or a Bayesian TPE sampler) proposes parameter sets, a Snakemake pipeline executes PureCLIP and scores the result against three biological quality signals, and the optimizer iterates toward the highest composite score. The two optimizers share identical evaluation and objective code so their results are directly comparable.

components.name: IP Replicate BAM Files
components.description: Pre-aligned, deduplicated eCLIP immunoprecipitation reads for the target RBP. At least two biological replicates are required. Reads from reverse transcription truncations mark RNA–protein crosslink sites at near-nucleotide resolution.
outputs: Aligned, deduplicated BAM files (one per IP replicate)

components.name: SMInput Control BAM
components.description: Size-matched input control: the same protocol without specific antibody enrichment. Used by PureCLIP as a covariate to model non-specific background signal.
outputs: Aligned, deduplicated BAM file (single control)

components.name: Reference Genome (GRCh38)
components.description: GRCh38 primary assembly FASTA. Required by PureCLIP for coordinate context and by the scorer to extract flanking nucleotide sequences around binding sites for motif analysis.
outputs: FASTA file + samtools .fai index

components.name: ENCODE Reference Binding Regions
components.description: Curated set of high-confidence binding regions from ENCODE for the target RBP and cell line. Acts as a ground-truth proxy for computing benchmark recall. Restricted to analyzed chromosomes under chr21 fast mode.
outputs: BED6 file of known strong binding regions

components.name: RBP Motif PWM Files
components.description: Position weight matrices in TRANSFAC format, organized by database (mCrossBase, ATtRACT, CISBP-RNA, RBPDB, RBPmap, oRNAment), RBP, and cell line. Used by the scorer to compute motif hit rates. IUPAC consensus strings serve as fallback.
outputs: TRANSFAC-format .transfac files under data/motifs/{db}/{rbp}/{cell_line}/

components.name: Run Configuration (run_config.yaml)
components.description: The single source of truth for one optimization trial: dataset identity, BAM paths, genome path, benchmark paths, all PureCLIP parameters, all postprocessing parameters, output paths, resource limits, and prior knowledge (known motifs, objective weights). Written by the optimizer before every trial; read by Snakemake and the scorer.
outputs: YAML file consumed by the Snakemake workflow and scorer
adjustable_parameters: pureclip.bandwidth_nt [20–100]: Gaussian kernel bandwidth for HMM state emission smoothing
pureclip.merge_distance_nt [4–16]: Max gap to merge adjacent crosslink sites into a binding region
pureclip.high_precision_mode {0,1}: Toggle stricter HMM state transitions
pureclip.use_input_covariate {0,1}: Whether to model SMInput as a background covariate
postprocessing.min_crosslink_events [2–6]: Minimum crosslink events required to retain a region
postprocessing.force_width [3–15]: Standardized output site width in nt (centered on region summit)
postprocessing.cluster_gap_width [4–16]: Gap allowed when clustering sites

components.name: samtools merge
components.description: Merges the per-replicate IP BAM files into a single pooled BAM. PureCLIP is run on this merged file to produce the final binding site calls, and separately on each replicate for reproducibility scoring.
outputs: merged_ip.bam + .bai index

components.name: PureCLIP (pureclip2 fork)
components.description: HMM-based peak caller for eCLIP data. Models crosslink-truncation enrichment over a background (optionally the SMInput), emitting crosslink sites and merging them into binding regions. Run once on the merged BAM (final calls) and once per replicate (for reproducibility scoring). Treat as a black box: provide BAMs and parameters, receive BED output.
inputs: Merged IP BAM (or per-replicate IP BAM)
outputs: PureCLIP.crosslink_sites.bed: individual crosslink site calls (BED)
PureCLIP.binding_regions.bed: merged binding regions (BED, name field encodes crosslink events)
adjustable_parameters: bandwidth_nt: Gaussian smoothing kernel width (narrower = sharper peaks, may miss broad binding)
merge_distance_nt: Distance threshold for merging nearby crosslink sites into one binding region
high_precision_mode: Stricter state-transition probabilities for higher specificity
use_input_covariate: Conditions the emission model on the SMInput BAM to suppress background

components.name: Postprocessor (workflow/postprocess.py)
components.description: Normalizes raw PureCLIP binding regions to a standardized footprint for downstream analysis. Filters by region length and crosslink event count, then re-centers each surviving region to a fixed width around its summit.
outputs: binding_sites.reproducible.bed: filtered and width-normalized binding sites
adjustable_parameters: min_region_length_nt: Discard regions shorter than this
min_crosslink_events: Discard regions with fewer crosslink events (parsed from semicolon-delimited BED name field)
force_width: Output site width in nt
components.project_math: 1. Filter: retain region if (end - start) >= min_region_length_nt. 2. Filter: retain region if count(';'-delimited name tokens) >= min_crosslink_events. 3. For each surviving region: summit = (start + end) // 2; new_start = max(0, summit - force_width // 2); new_end = new_start + force_width.

components.name: Scorer (scorers/run_scorers.py)
components.description: Computes three biological quality signals for a set of binding sites and writes score_report.json. All tools used for interval operations (bedtools intersect, shuffle, getfasta) are treated as black-box utilities.
inputs: Per-replicate PureCLIP binding regions BED files
Reference genome FASTA (for sequence extraction and shuffle genome sizes)
outputs: score_report.json containing: n_binding_sites, replicate_agreement, reproducibility_score, motif_hit_rate, motif_enrichment, benchmark_region_recall, and the params that produced them
adjustable_parameters: flank_nt=15: nt flanking window around each site for motif sequence extraction
threshold_pct=0.80: PWM score threshold as fraction of (max - min) log-odds range
n_shuffles=3: Number of random permutations used to estimate chance-level agreement

project_math.replicate_agreement: observed = (sites in binding_sites.bed overlapping EVERY per-replicate regions BED) / total_sites. Uses chained bedtools intersect -u calls, one per replicate.
project_math.reproducibility_score: expected = mean replicate_agreement over n_shuffles=3 random permutations of binding sites (each site relocated randomly within its own chromosome via bedtools shuffle -chrom). score = clamp((observed - expected) / (1 - expected), 0, 1). Chance-corrects for broad intervals that trivially overlap.
project_math.pwm_log_odds: For each position p in the PWM and each base b: log_odds[p][b] = log2( (freq[p][b] / row_total + 0.01) / (1 + 4*0.01) / 0.25 ). Pseudocount=0.01, background=0.25 (uniform). Best score for a sequence = max over all offsets of sum of log_odds[i][seq[offset+i]].
project_math.motif_hit_rate: 1. Extract ±15 nt windows around each binding site (bedtools getfasta -s). 2. For each PWM: threshold = min_score + 0.80*(max_score - min_score); fg_rate = fraction of site windows with best_score >= threshold; bg_rate = same on per-sequence character-shuffled copies (preserves base composition). enrichment = fg_rate / bg_rate. 3. Report fg_rate of the PWM with the highest enrichment.
project_math.benchmark_recall: recall = (ENCODE reference regions with ≥1 overlap in binding sites) / total reference regions, restricted to analyzed chromosomes (chr21 only in fast mode). Uses bedtools intersect -u.

components.name: Composite Objective (agent/decisions.py)
components.description: Single source-of-truth scoring function that reduces the three scorer signals to one [0,1] value the optimizers maximize. Imported by both optimizers and the monitor so all components use an identical formula.
outputs: Scalar composite score in [0, 1]
adjustable_parameters: weights.reproducibility (default 0.5)
weights.motif (default 0.25)
weights.recall (default 0.25)
min_sites (default 10): site count below which yield_factor ramps score toward 0
components.project_math: terms = {k: v for k, v in {reproducibility: reproducibility_score (fallback: replicate_agreement), motif: motif_hit_rate, recall: benchmark_region_recall} if v is not None}. total_w = sum(weights[k] for k in terms). base = sum(weights[k] * terms[k] for k in terms) / total_w. yield_factor = min(1.0, max(0, n_binding_sites) / min_sites). composite = base * yield_factor. Weights are renormalised over whichever terms are present in the report.

components.name: evaluate_config (agent/evaluation.py)
components.description: Shared evaluation harness used by both optimizers. Validates the proposed config, writes it to disk, invokes the Snakemake DAG (forcing the PureCLIP and postprocess rules to rerun), runs the scorer, and returns the parsed score_report dict.
outputs: Parsed score_report dict
adjustable_parameters: FORCE_RULES = ['pureclip', 'pureclip_per_replicate', 'postprocess']: Rules always re-executed so parameter changes take effect

components.name: LLM Optimizer (agent/graph.py)
components.description: LangGraph state machine that uses DeepSeek (deepseek-chat, temperature=0.2) to propose parameter changes. The LLM receives the full iteration history with per-step deltas and biological priors, and must return a JSON object naming one parameter change and its reasoning. Invalid or repeated proposals are re-prompted up to MAX_DECISION_RETRIES=3 times before the run converges.
outputs: Updated run_config.yaml (new parameter set for next trial)
decisions.jsonl entries: {iteration, params, scores, composite, reasoning, changes}
adjustable_parameters: MAX_ITER: number of optimization iterations
MAX_DECISION_RETRIES=3: re-prompt attempts before accepting stale config
model: deepseek-chat (configurable via ChatOpenAI constructor)
temperature=0.2
objective_weights (via priors.json)
components.project_math: Prompt includes: current composite score, per-iteration table of {params, reproducibility, motif_hit_rate, known_site_recall, n_sites, composite, d_reproducibility, d_recall, d_composite}. LLM responds with JSON {reasoning, changes: {pureclip: {param: value}, postprocessing: {param: value}}}. Changes validated against search bounds and checked against tried_signatures (JSON-serialized tunable snapshot set) to prevent repeats.

components.name: Optuna Optimizer (agent/optuna_runner.py)
components.description: Bayesian optimization using Optuna's TPE (Tree-structured Parzen Estimator) sampler. Requires no API key. Each trial suggests integer values for all tunable parameters within their bounds, calls evaluate_config, and returns composite_objective as the trial value.
outputs: config/best_config.yaml: config of the highest-scoring trial
decisions.jsonl entries: {iteration, optimizer: 'optuna', params, scores, composite, reasoning: 'TPE proposal', changes: null}
adjustable_parameters: n_trials (MAX_ITER env var, default 12)
sampler: TPESampler (seed=42)
search_bounds: per-parameter integer ranges
components.project_math: For each trial: suggest_int(section.key, low, high) for all parameters in search_bounds. Apply to base config. Score = composite_objective(evaluate_config(config), weights). TPE builds separate Parzen-window density models l(x) (good trials) and g(x) (bad trials) and samples from argmax(l(x)/g(x)). Direction: maximize.

components.name: Overnight Batch Runner (scripts/overnight_batch.py)
components.description: Failure-tolerant multi-job runner. Iterates through a YAML manifest of jobs, launches each as an isolated subprocess within a wall-clock budget, and records all outcomes regardless of individual failures. Never aborts the batch on a single job failure.
inputs: Batch manifest YAML (list of jobs with dataset, optimizer, MAX_ITER, etc.)
outputs: results/overnight/iterations.jsonl: one row per scored iteration (metrics + params + composite)
results/overnight/jobs.jsonl: one row per job (status, timing, exit code, failure hint)
results/overnight/summary.csv: one row per job with best composite + status
results/overnight/<job_id>/: per-job run_config, per-iteration results, run log
adjustable_parameters: --hours: wall-clock budget
--no-repeat: skip jobs already completed
--pureclip-dir: path prepended to PATH for pureclip2 binary

components.name: Monitor + REST API (scripts/monitor.py)
components.description: Python stdlib HTTP server exposing a REST API over the results/overnight/ output files and serving the compiled React SPA. Imports composite_objective directly so dashboard scores are always computed with the live objective formula.
outputs: GET /api/runs: list of all runs with best scores and metadata
GET /api/run/<id>: iteration-level details for one run
GET /api/status: active job and queue state
POST /api/schedule: enqueue a new job
Static SPA serving on /
adjustable_parameters: --port (default 8888)

components.name: Dashboard UI (ui/)
components.description: React Router v8 SPA with four pages. Built with React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, and Vite. In development proxies /api to monitor.py; in production served as a static build by monitor.py.
outputs: Browser-rendered experiment dashboard

pages.Dashboard: Active run stepper + LLM-vs-Optuna leaderboard. Composite scores re-derived client-side from raw metrics via the same formula.
pages.Runs: Per-iteration decision trail: params changed and LLM reasoning, sourced from decisions.jsonl via /api/run/<id>.
pages.Plan run: Form to pick dataset, parameter ranges, optimizer type; submits POST /api/schedule.
pages.Variables: Plain-English descriptions of all tunable parameters and their biological effects.
